eli5.text: The program now checks the assistant's list a different way when it starts up: instead of peeking at what gets printed to your screen, it reads the list directly to confirm your named assistant appears. You wouldn't see anything new in the program itself, but the behind-the-scenes check that runs each time you start the program has been made simpler and less fragile, so it is less likely to break from a future display change. This only affects the startup step and is already live today.

ai.title: CLI renderer cleanup writes terminal reset escape sequences before
ai.summary: renderer-cleanup.ts adds resetTerminalState() to write raw ANSI escape sequences to stdout before renderer.destroy(). This disables X10, button, and SGR mouse modes, focus reporting, and bracketed paste, while showing the cursor. The change ensures terminal state resets even if the renderer fails or on Windows where SIGTERM/SIGHUP are unavailable. Scope limited to cli/src/utils/renderer-cleanup.ts.

eli5.text: When you finish using the command-line tool and it closes, your terminal now resets itself to a clean state first. This means you'll notice that mouse selections, paste shortcuts, and other interactive features go back to normal behavior even if the program was stuck or on Windows (where the usual shutdown signals don't work). It works by sending hidden cleanup messages directly to your terminal before the program fully exits, ensuring they get through even if something went wrong during shutdown. This is live today for command-line users on all platforms.

eli5.text: When you see an advertisement banner in the app, the button text now comes from a dedicated 'call to action' field if the ad has one, otherwise it falls back to the ad's title, and finally to 'Learn more' if neither is available. This means advertisers can now control the exact text on the button (like 'Shop now' or 'Sign up') instead of relying on the title, which might have been too long or not button-friendly. The change is live today for anyone seeing ads in the app, and if you looked at an ad banner you'd just notice the button text may be different or more specifically chosen than before.

ai.title: Gravity ad payload moves message filtering to server
ai.summary: CLI `use-gravity-ad.ts` now sends full `adMessages` to `/api/v1/ads`, removing client-side selection of last user/assistant messages. Server `web/src/app/api/v1/ads/_post.ts` handles filtering, stripping `<user_message>` tags via `extractLastUserMessageContent`, and selecting the last assistant message preceding the last user message. Scope covers CLI hook and web API route. Request body now includes `userId` and `user.email` from `userInfo`.

eli5.text: When the assistant shows you an ad after a response, the app now sends your full recent chat history to its servers instead of pre-picking just the last two messages on your device. The server then decides which messages matter, stripping out internal formatting from your last question and picking the assistant's reply, so you get the same ad relevance without that work happening locally on your computer.

ai.title: Ads API includes render context and device targeting
ai.summary: Ads API requests now include `renderContext` with fixed placement and length constraints, plus optional `device` targeting data. CLI sends OS, timezone, and locale derived from Node.js process and Intl APIs. Server extracts client IP from `x-forwarded-for` or `x-real-ip` headers to populate device context. Changes affect `cli/src/hooks/use-gravity-ad.ts` and `web/src/app/api/v1/ads/_post.ts`.

eli5.text: When the assistant asks its ad service for an ad to show you, the request now carries information about your device, such as whether you're on a Mac, Windows, or Linux computer, along with your time zone and language. This lets the ad system pick ads that are more relevant to you. You won't see this information yourself, but it helps the assistant serve better-targeted content.

ai.title: CLI settings create config dir on first load
ai.summary: Added `ensureConfigDirExists` helper in `cli/src/utils/settings.ts`. `loadSettings` now calls it before writing the default `settings.json`, preventing errors when the config directory is missing. `saveSettings` refactored to use the same helper instead of inline `mkdirSync` logic.

eli5.text: When the CLI first runs and needs to save your settings, it now automatically creates the folder that holds your settings before trying to write the file, instead of failing if that folder doesn't exist yet. You'd notice this only if you previously saw an error about a missing folder the first time the tool tried to save your preferences; now that step just works. The same folder-check logic is reused whenever you save settings, removing duplicated code that did the same thing a different way. This is already live for anyone using the CLI today.

ai.summary: The CLI `use-gravity-ad` hook now sources `sessionId` from `useChatStore.getState().chatSessionId` rather than `loggerContext.clientSessionId`. This aligns ad tracking with the active chat session, which is regenerated on `/new` via `crypto.randomUUID()` in `chat-store.ts`. The change also updates the Web API `postAds` endpoint to include `supports_links`, `supports_markdown`, and `numAds: 1` in the Gravity API request payload.

eli5.text: Ads shown in your chat now match the current conversation. Each time you start a new chat, a fresh tracking ID is assigned, so ad activity is tied to that specific session rather than a general session ID. The system also requests one ad at a time and lets the ad service know whether the response supports clickable links. This takes effect today for everyone using the CLI.

ai.title: Version 1.0.582 release bundling ads, CLI, and logging changes
ai.summary: Release 1.0.582 increments the version in cli/release/package.json from 1.0.581 and aggregates previously landed changes across the CLI and ads surfaces. Notables include the new Clickable component and CopyButton refactor in cli/src/components, the dedicated cta field on ad impressions with migration 0034_orange_firebrand.sql adding a non-null cta column to the ad_impression table, ads defaulting on for new users with /ads:enable and /ads:disable exiting beta, server-side message filtering moving to web/src/app/api/v1/ads/_post.ts, and device targeting adding renderContext plus OS/timezone/locale from the CLI. CLI quality-of-life fixes include resetTerminalState() writing ANSI reset sequences before renderer.destroy() in cli/src/utils/renderer-cleanup.ts, ensureConfigDirExists in cli/src/utils/settings.ts preventing missing config directory errors, announceLoadedAgents using logger.debug instead of console.log in cli/src/utils/local-agent-registry.ts, and the publish command routing through logger.info/error/warn in cli/src/index.tsx.
ai.evidence: The diff modifies cli/release/package.json, incrementing the version field from 1.0.581 to 1.0.582 with a single +1/-1 line change. The release context shows this is a version bump aggregating prior changes in ads (cta field, default-on, server-side message filtering, device targeting, chat session ID), CLI improvements (Clickable component, CopyButton refactor, structured logging, terminal reset on cleanup, config dir creation), and the announceLoadedAgents logger.debug migration.

eli5.text: This release brings you more useful ads and a smoother terminal experience. You will now see ads enabled by default when you first install the app, and each ad includes a clear call-to-action button telling you what the ad offers. When you click things like copy buttons in the terminal, the text will no longer get accidentally highlighted while you click. The app now handles errors and status messages in a cleaner, easier-to-read way by switching from basic text output to structured logging across commands and agent loading. Terminal cleanup has also been improved so your terminal returns to its normal state even if something goes wrong. Finally, settings setup is more reliable because the app now automatically creates the folder it needs to store your configuration on first run.

ai.title: CLI logout deletes web sessions; auth refactor
ai.summary: CLI logout now deletes associated web sessions and unclaims fingerprints. New `_db.ts` and `_post.ts` modules in `web/src/app/api/auth/cli/logout/` handle session cleanup and fingerprint state. `auth-options.ts` uses `SESSION_MAX_AGE_SECONDS` constant. Onboarding logic moved to `web/src/app/onboard/_db.ts` with replay attack check.

eli5.text: When you sign out of the CLI tool, the system now also clears your web-based login sessions and releases any device identifiers tied to that account, so your online and command-line presences are fully disconnected in one action. This affects anyone who logs in through the terminal and then uses the same account in a browser. If you were to look, you'd see the logout endpoint returning a cleaner state where no lingering web sessions remain attached to your identity. Behind the scenes, the authentication logic was reorganized into dedicated modules for session and onboarding handling, but you won't notice that unless you're managing the codebase.

eli5.text: The app now defines two fixed time limits for how long your login session can last, about 30 days for keeping you signed in, and about 30 minutes for matching new activity to your session when the app tries to recognize your device. These values are stored as background settings that the app's code can use to keep your session behavior consistent, so you should notice nothing new right now since these limits were already handled elsewhere, they've just been gathered into one clearly labeled spot for the team to maintain.

ai.title: Add session createdat column for CLI logout time-window deletion
ai.summary: Migration `0035_warm_orphan.sql` adds `created_at` timestamp column to `session` table with `DEFAULT now()`. Enables time-window deletion strategy for CLI logout flow. Updates `schema.ts`, `_db.ts`, `_post.ts` in logout API. Covers packages/internal and web auth surfaces.

eli5.text: When you sign out of the command-line version of the app, the system now knows exactly when each login session (token) was created, because every session gets a timestamp the moment it starts. That timestamp lets the logout process quietly retire only the sessions that are still within a safe deletion window around the moment you signed out, instead of guessing which ones to touch. For you, this means signing out on the command line cleans up your active sessions more precisely, and you won't be accidentally signed out of a session that is clearly outside that window.

ai.title: Add /api/agents/metrics endpoint for client-side metrics loading
ai.summary: New GET /api/agents/metrics route serves cached agent metrics separately from the store page's initial SSR payload. Store page now fetches only basic agent info via getCachedAgentsBasicInfo, while client-side queries load metrics from the new endpoint and merge them. Covers web/src/app/api/agents/metrics/route.ts, store/page.tsx, store-client.tsx, agents-data.ts, and agents-transform.ts. Metrics response keyed by publisherId/agentName; basic info dedupes to latest version per agent and sorts alphabetically, leaving metrics-based sorting to the client.

eli5.text: The agents store page now loads with just basic agent info upfront, then pulls in usage metrics like run counts and spending separately after the page is already showing. If you visit the store, you'll see agent listings appear faster with less data transferred on the first load, while popularity and usage stats still fill in as before but through a dedicated metrics endpoint that serves cached data. The change is live today for the store page and affects anyone browsing the agent directory, with metrics now cached for ten minutes server-side to keep response times quick.
